key_insight: ZFO decouples optimizer direction from step-size by using first-order gradients for direction and cheap zeroth-order evaluations to adaptively choose the step length along that direction.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical, low-overhead alternative to full line search for LLM fine-tuning, improving stability and convergence without adding many objective evaluations.
method: Use a trusted first-order optimizer to propose the descent direction.
Evaluate the objective at two extra points along that direction to build a local 1D model.
Select a curvature-aware step within a bounded interval using shared-sample finite differences.
evidence_signal: Across multiple language-model and dataset settings, the method often outperformed fixed-step first-order baselines in both optimization behavior and final performance.
watch_item: The gains depend on the objective and local model choice, so implementation details and tuning of the bounded search interval may affect robustness.
paper_title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
